newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Ex-Miss Universe leads Venezuela presidential poll.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Miss Universe leads Venezuela presidential poll.

text.p: If a presidential election were held in Venezuela this week, former Miss Universe Irene Saez would comfortably land the country's top job, according to an opinion poll published on Tuesday.

Saez, 35, the mayor of Caracas district Chacao, was the preferred candidate of 45.3 percent of those quizzed by local pollsters Datanalisis as to who they would vote for if elections were held on July 6.
Venezuela's next presidential election is set for December 1998 and Saez has held a comfortable lead in polls for more than a year.
Her nearest rival, former Carabobo state governor Henrique Salas Romer, trailed with 13.2 percent of the 1,000 people surveyed, the poll published in El Nacional showed.

Claudio Fermin, a candidate for Democratic Action (AD) in 1993 elections had 10.2 percent of the vote and Hugo Chavez, a retired army officer who staged a failed coup attempt in 1992, had 8.2 percent.

Political analysts say her popularity stems from high public recognition. In addition, she has served two successful terms as mayor of Chacao during which the crime rate has dropped and public services have improved.
Although she has not officially declared her candidacy, Saez recently registered her political movement Integration, Representation, New Hope (IRENE) with election officials.
No margin of error was given for the poll.
